/-!
# The kernel-flattening brick (certificate clauses (c3)/(c4), G-4)

**Pure commutative algebra** (mathlib-only imports; no project geometry). Two layers:

## The fibrewise-injectivity engine (`ψ : P → N` injective on every residue fibre)

For a linear map `ψ : P →ₗ[R] N` with `P` finite (resp. finitely presented) and `N` finite
flat, such that `ψ ⊗ κ(p)` is injective for **every** prime `p`:

* `Module.Projective.of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective` — `P` is projective;
* `LinearMap.injective_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective` — `ψ` is injective;
* `Module.Flat.quotient_range_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective` —
  `N ⧸ range ψ` is flat.

Route: at each maximal ideal, `ψ` localizes to a **split** injection between a finite and
a finite free module over the local ring
(`IsLocalRing.split_injective_iff_lTensor_residueField_injective`, with the cokernel free
by `Module.free_of_lTensor_residueField_injective` — Matsumura 22.5-style, but with an
elementary basis-lifting proof in mathlib, no local criterion of flatness);
projectivity, injectivity and flatness then globalize
(`Module.projective_of_localization_maximal`, `injective_of_localized_maximal`,
`Module.flat_of_localized_maximal`). The residue fibre of the localized map is identified
with the original residue fibre through `LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct` and
`AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange` (`residueFieldLocEquiv`).

## The kernel-flattening keystones (the (c3)/(c4) table row of `w4-g4-worksheet` §3)

For `f : M →ₗ[R] N` between finite flat modules over a **Noetherian** `R` and a submodule
`L ≤ ker f` whose residue-fibre images span every fibre kernel —

`hspan : ∀ p, ker (f ⊗ κ(p)) ≤ range (L.subtype ⊗ κ(p))`

(the **fibrewise-spanning** hypothesis; the fibre kernels are spanned by *relative* elements)
— the k[ε]-trap is ruled out and the naive constant-fibre-rank pin becomes true:

* `Module.Projective.quotient_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le` — `M ⧸ L` projective;
* `Submodule.eq_ker_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le` — `L = ker f`;
* `Module.Flat.quotient_ker_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le` — `M ⧸ ker f` flat (**c3**);
* `Module.Flat.quotient_range_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le` — `N ⧸ range f` flat (**c4**);
* `Module.Projective.ker_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le` — `ker f` finite projective
  (finiteness is automatic: submodule of a finite module over a Noetherian ring);
* `LinearMap.rTensor_subtype_injective_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le` and
  `LinearMap.range_rTensor_subtype_eq_ker_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le` — formation
  of `ker f` commutes with residue fields: `L ⊗ κ(p) ≅ ker (f ⊗ κ(p))`;
* `Module.rankAtStalk_ker_eq_finrank_ker_baseChange` /
  `Module.rankAtStalk_ker_eq_of_forall_finrank_eq` — `rankAtStalk (ker f) p` equals the
  fibre-kernel dimension (`= g` when the fibres are `g`-dimensional) (**c2** rank clause).

Route: `hspan` says exactly that the induced map `M ⧸ L → N` is injective on every residue
fibre (right-exactness of `− ⊗ κ(p)`), so the engine applies to it; `L = ker f` and the split
SES `0 → L → M → M ⧸ L → 0` (projective quotient) give the rest.

## The `k[ε]` guard

Constant fibre-kernel dimension alone is FALSE: `R = k[ε]`, `f = (ε •) : R → R` has
`ker (f ⊗ κ) = κ` at the unique prime (constant dimension 1), but `ker f = (ε)` is not
projective and `R ⧸ (ε)` is not flat. `hspan` fails there: every element of `(ε)` maps to
zero in the fibre `R ⊗ κ = k`, so the fibre kernel is *not* spanned by relative elements.
Any weakening of `hspan` must keep this example excluded.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u v w

open scoped TensorProduct

/-! ## Residue fibres of localized modules -/

section LocalizedFibre

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]

/-- The residue fibre of the localized module at `q` is the residue fibre of the module:
`κ(q) ⊗[R_q] X_q ≃ κ(q) ⊗[R] X`. -/
private noncomputable def residueFieldLocEquiv (q : Ideal R) [q.IsPrime]
    (X : Type*) [AddCommGroup X] [Module R X] :
    q.ResidueField ⊗[Localization.AtPrime q] LocalizedModule q.primeCompl X
      ≃ₗ[q.ResidueField] q.ResidueField ⊗[R] X :=
  (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.congr
      (LinearEquiv.refl q.ResidueField q.ResidueField)
      (LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct q.primeCompl X)) ≪≫ₗ
    TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange R (Localization.AtPrime q)
      q.ResidueField q.ResidueField X

/-- Naturality of `residueFieldLocEquiv` against `LocalizedModule.map`. -/
private lemma residueFieldLocEquiv_map {X : Type v} {Y : Type w}
    [AddCommGroup X] [Module R X] [AddCommGroup Y] [Module R Y]
    (q : Ideal R) [q.IsPrime] (φ : X →ₗ[R] Y)
    (t : q.ResidueField ⊗[Localization.AtPrime q] LocalizedModule q.primeCompl X) :
    residueFieldLocEquiv q Y
        (((LocalizedModule.map q.primeCompl φ).lTensor q.ResidueField) t)
      = (φ.lTensor q.ResidueField) (residueFieldLocEquiv q X t) := by
  induction t with
  | zero => simp
  | tmul c x =>
      induction x using LocalizedModule.induction_on with
      | _ m s =>
          simp [residueFieldLocEquiv, LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct_apply_mk]
  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]

/-- Fibrewise injectivity transports to the localized map: if `φ ⊗ κ(q)` is injective, so
is `κ(q) ⊗ (φ_q)`. -/
private lemma injective_lTensor_residueField_localizedMap {X : Type v} {Y : Type w}
    [AddCommGroup X] [Module R X] [AddCommGroup Y] [Module R Y]
    (q : Ideal R) [q.IsPrime] (φ : X →ₗ[R] Y)
    (hfib : Function.Injective (φ.rTensor q.ResidueField)) :
    Function.Injective ((LocalizedModule.map q.primeCompl φ).lTensor q.ResidueField) := by
  have hl : Function.Injective (φ.lTensor q.ResidueField) :=
    (LinearMap.lTensor_inj_iff_rTensor_inj _ _).mpr hfib
  intro a b hab
  refine (residueFieldLocEquiv q X).injective (hl ?_)
  rw [← residueFieldLocEquiv_map q φ a, ← residueFieldLocEquiv_map q φ b, hab]

end LocalizedFibre

/-! ## The fibrewise-injectivity engine -/

section FibrewiseInjective

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
variable {P : Type v} {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]

/-- The local heart: at a maximal ideal, a fibrewise-injective map from a finite module to
a finite flat module localizes to a **split** injection. -/
private lemma exists_comp_localizedMap_eq_id [Module.Finite R P] [Module.Finite R N]
    [Module.Flat R N] (ψ : P →ₗ[R] N) (J : Ideal R) [J.IsMaximal]
    (hfib : Function.Injective (ψ.rTensor J.ResidueField)) :
    ∃ l' : LocalizedModule J.primeCompl N →ₗ[Localization.AtPrime J]
        LocalizedModule J.primeCompl P,
      l' ∘ₗ LocalizedModule.map J.primeCompl ψ = LinearMap.id := by
  haveI : Module.Finite (Localization.AtPrime J) (LocalizedModule J.primeCompl P) :=
    Module.Finite.of_isLocalizedModule J.primeCompl (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap J.primeCompl P)
  haveI : Module.Finite (Localization.AtPrime J) (LocalizedModule J.primeCompl N) :=
    Module.Finite.of_isLocalizedModule J.primeCompl (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap J.primeCompl N)
  haveI : Module.Free (Localization.AtPrime J) (LocalizedModule J.primeCompl N) :=
    Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing
  exact (IsLocalRing.split_injective_iff_lTensor_residueField_injective
    (LocalizedModule.map J.primeCompl ψ)).mpr
    (injective_lTensor_residueField_localizedMap J ψ hfib)

/-- **Fibrewise injective into finite flat ⟹ projective**: a finitely presented module
admitting a linear map to a finite flat module that is injective on every residue-field
fibre is projective (hence flat). Mathlib-general; no Noetherian hypothesis. -/
theorem Module.Projective.of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective
    [Module.FinitePresentation R P] [Module.Finite R N] [Module.Flat R N] (ψ : P →ₗ[R] N)
    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      Function.Injective (ψ.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    Module.Projective R P := by
  refine Module.projective_of_localization_maximal (fun J hJ => ?_)
  haveI : Module.Projective (Localization.AtPrime J) (LocalizedModule J.primeCompl N) := by
    haveI : Module.Finite (Localization.AtPrime J) (LocalizedModule J.primeCompl N) :=
      Module.Finite.of_isLocalizedModule J.primeCompl
        (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap J.primeCompl N)
    haveI : Module.Free (Localization.AtPrime J) (LocalizedModule J.primeCompl N) :=
      Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing
    infer_instance
  obtain ⟨l', hl'⟩ := exists_comp_localizedMap_eq_id ψ J (hfib ⟨J, hJ.isPrime⟩)
  exact Module.Projective.of_split _ _ hl'

/-- **Fibrewise injective ⟹ injective** for a map from a finite module to a finite flat
module (injectivity is checked at maximal localizations, where the map splits). -/
theorem LinearMap.injective_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective
    [Module.Finite R P] [Module.Finite R N] [Module.Flat R N] (ψ : P →ₗ[R] N)
    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      Function.Injective (ψ.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    Function.Injective ψ := by
  apply injective_of_localized_maximal
  intro J hJ
  obtain ⟨l', hl'⟩ := exists_comp_localizedMap_eq_id ψ J (hfib ⟨J, hJ.isPrime⟩)
  exact Function.HasLeftInverse.injective ⟨l', LinearMap.congr_fun hl'⟩

/-- **Fibrewise injective ⟹ flat cokernel**: for `ψ : P → N` with `P` finite, `N` finite
flat and `ψ ⊗ κ(p)` injective at every prime, the cokernel `N ⧸ range ψ` is flat (locally
it is even free, by `Module.free_of_lTensor_residueField_injective`). -/
theorem Module.Flat.quotient_range_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective
    [Module.Finite R P] [Module.Finite R N] [Module.Flat R N] (ψ : P →ₗ[R] N)
    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      Function.Injective (ψ.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range ψ) := by
  apply Module.flat_of_localized_maximal
  intro J hJ
  haveI : Module.Finite (Localization.AtPrime J) (LocalizedModule J.primeCompl P) :=
    Module.Finite.of_isLocalizedModule J.primeCompl (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap J.primeCompl P)
  haveI : Module.Finite (Localization.AtPrime J) (LocalizedModule J.primeCompl N) :=
    Module.Finite.of_isLocalizedModule J.primeCompl (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap J.primeCompl N)
  haveI : Module.Free (Localization.AtPrime J) (LocalizedModule J.primeCompl N) :=
    Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing
  haveI : Module.Free (Localization.AtPrime J)
      (LocalizedModule J.primeCompl (N ⧸ LinearMap.range ψ)) :=
    Module.free_of_lTensor_residueField_injective
      (LocalizedModule.map J.primeCompl ψ)
      (LocalizedModule.map J.primeCompl (LinearMap.range ψ).mkQ)
      (LocalizedModule.map_surjective _ _ (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _))
      (LocalizedModule.map_exact _ _ _ ψ.exact_map_mkQ_range)
      (injective_lTensor_residueField_localizedMap J ψ (hfib ⟨J, hJ.isPrime⟩))
  exact Module.Flat.trans R (Localization.AtPrime J) _

end FibrewiseInjective

/-! ## The kernel-flattening keystones -/

section KernelFlattening

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
variable {M : Type v} {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
variable [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Finite R N] [Module.Flat R N]
variable (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (L : Submodule R M)

omit [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Finite R N] [Module.Flat R N] in
/-- `f` kills `L` as a composite. -/
private lemma comp_subtype_eq_zero (hle : L ≤ LinearMap.ker f) : f ∘ₗ L.subtype = 0 :=
  LinearMap.ext fun x => LinearMap.mem_ker.mp (hle x.2)

omit [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Finite R N] [Module.Flat R N] in
/-- The fibrewise-spanning hypothesis says exactly that the induced map
`M ⧸ L → N` is injective on every residue-field fibre (right-exactness of `− ⊗ κ(p)`). -/
private lemma liftQ_rTensor_residueField_injective (hle : L ≤ LinearMap.ker f)
    (hspan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≤
        LinearMap.range ((L.subtype).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
    Function.Injective ((L.liftQ f hle).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
  rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
  intro t ht
  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := LinearMap.rTensor_surjective p.asIdeal.ResidueField
    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L) t
  have hy : y ∈ LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
    rw [LinearMap.mem_ker, ← L.liftQ_mkQ f hle, LinearMap.rTensor_comp, LinearMap.comp_apply]
    exact ht
  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := hspan p hy
  exact (rTensor_exact p.asIdeal.ResidueField (LinearMap.exact_subtype_mkQ L)
    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L) y).mpr ⟨u, hu⟩

/-- **The flattening keystone, quotient form**: over a Noetherian ring, if the residue
fibres of the kernel of `f : M → N` (`M` finite, `N` finite flat) are spanned by a
submodule `L ≤ ker f`, then `M ⧸ L` is finite projective (in particular flat). -/
theorem Module.Projective.quotient_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le
    (hle : L ≤ LinearMap.ker f)
    (hspan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≤
        LinearMap.range ((L.subtype).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    Module.Projective R (M ⧸ L) := by
  haveI : Module.FinitePresentation R (M ⧸ L) := Module.finitePresentation_of_finite R _
  exact Module.Projective.of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective (L.liftQ f hle)
    (liftQ_rTensor_residueField_injective f L hle hspan)

omit [IsNoetherianRing R] in
/-- **The kernel is no larger than its fibrewise-spanning submodule**: `L = ker f`. This is
the relative-elements completeness clause (conclusion (4) of the G-4 brick). -/
theorem Submodule.eq_ker_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le
    (hle : L ≤ LinearMap.ker f)
    (hspan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≤
        LinearMap.range ((L.subtype).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    L = LinearMap.ker f := by
  refine le_antisymm hle fun x hx => ?_
  have hinj : Function.Injective (L.liftQ f hle) :=
    LinearMap.injective_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective (L.liftQ f hle)
      (liftQ_rTensor_residueField_injective f L hle hspan)
  have h0 : L.liftQ f hle (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) = 0 := by
    rw [Submodule.liftQ_apply]
    exact LinearMap.mem_ker.mp hx
  have hmk : (Submodule.Quotient.mk x : M ⧸ L) = 0 := hinj (by rw [h0, map_zero])
  rwa [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero] at hmk

/-- **Certificate clause (c3)**: `M ⧸ ker f` is flat (indeed projective, being `M ⧸ L`). -/
theorem Module.Flat.quotient_ker_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le
    (hle : L ≤ LinearMap.ker f)
    (hspan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≤
        LinearMap.range ((L.subtype).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    Module.Flat R (M ⧸ LinearMap.ker f) := by
  haveI := Module.Projective.quotient_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le f L hle hspan
  rw [← Submodule.eq_ker_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le f L hle hspan]
  infer_instance

omit [IsNoetherianRing R] in
/-- **Certificate clause (c4)**: `N ⧸ range f` is flat. -/
theorem Module.Flat.quotient_range_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le
    (hle : L ≤ LinearMap.ker f)
    (hspan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≤
        LinearMap.range ((L.subtype).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range f) := by
  have hrange : LinearMap.range f = LinearMap.range (L.liftQ f hle) :=
    (Submodule.range_liftQ L f hle).symm
  rw [hrange]
  exact Module.Flat.quotient_range_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective (L.liftQ f hle)
    (liftQ_rTensor_residueField_injective f L hle hspan)

/-- The split retraction of `L ↪ M` (from projectivity of `M ⧸ L`). -/
private lemma exists_comp_subtype_eq_id [Module.Flat R M] (hle : L ≤ LinearMap.ker f)
    (hspan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≤
        LinearMap.range ((L.subtype).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    ∃ r : M →ₗ[R] L, r ∘ₗ L.subtype = LinearMap.id := by
  haveI := Module.Projective.quotient_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le f L hle hspan
  obtain ⟨σ, hσ⟩ := Module.projective_lifting_property L.mkQ LinearMap.id
    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L)
  have hmem : ∀ x : M, x - σ (L.mkQ x) ∈ L := by
    intro x
    rw [← Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero, ← Submodule.mkQ_apply, map_sub]
    rw [show L.mkQ (σ (L.mkQ x)) = L.mkQ x from LinearMap.congr_fun hσ (L.mkQ x)]
    exact sub_self _
  refine ⟨(LinearMap.id - σ ∘ₗ L.mkQ).codRestrict L (fun x => by simpa using hmem x), ?_⟩
  ext x
  have hx0 : L.mkQ (x : M) = 0 := by
    rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
    exact x.2
  simp [hx0]

/-- The submodule `L` (equivalently `ker f`) is projective — with finiteness automatic over
the Noetherian base, this is the finite-projective half of certificate clause (c2). -/
theorem Module.Projective.ker_of_forall_ker_rTensor_residueField_le [Module.Flat R M]
    (hle : L ≤ LinearMap.ker f)
    (hspan : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≤
        LinearMap.range ((L.subtype).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    Module.Projective R (LinearMap.ker f) := by
  obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := exists_comp_subtype_eq_id f L hle hspan
  haveI : Module.Projective R M := by
    haveI := Module.finitePresentation_of_finite R M
    exact Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation

import Mathlib.RingTheory.Flat.Equalizer

/-!
# Base change of kernels and regular elements from flat cokernels (the `lm:ctn`-lite home)

Pure module algebra (no schemes), the shared Tor-lemma home of the DAT-D/DAT-A lanes
(`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §2; Kleiman `lm:ctn`, tex 1747–1815, made cheap by carrying
flatness as data). Everything here is applications of mathlib's purity gift
`LinearMap.lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat` (a short exact sequence with flat last
term stays left-exact under any `⊗`).

For a linear map `δ : M →ₗ[R] N` whose two cokernels are flat — `M ⧸ ker δ` (≅ the
image) and `N ⧸ range δ` — the kernel of `δ` commutes with arbitrary base change:

* `LinearMap.ker_lTensor_eq_of_flat_coker`: `ker (δ ⊗ A) = range ((ker δ).subtype ⊗ A)`
  for every module `A` (with the `Function.Exact` form
  `LinearMap.exact_lTensor_of_flat_coker`);
* `LinearMap.tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker` /
  `LinearMap.tensorKerEquivOfFlatCoker`: the canonical comparison map
  `LinearMap.tensorKer` — the SAME map as mathlib's flat-base-change case
  `LinearMap.tensorKerEquiv`, so downstream sees one seam with two sufficient
  conditions — is an isomorphism `R' ⊗[R] ker δ ≃ₗ[R'] ker (𝟙 ⊗ δ)`. The DD-1
  certificate consumes this on the glued colength module `W(d) = ker (δ⁻ − δ⁺)`, whose
  certificate clauses (c3)/(c4) are exactly the two flatness hypotheses.
* `Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_flat_coker`: a regular
  element `f ∈ B⁰` of an `R`-algebra with `B ⧸ (f)` flat over `R` stays regular in
  `R' ⊗[R] B` for every `R`-algebra `R'` — the DD-1a `hreg` discharge and the shape
  shared with DAT-A2's germ-regularity bridge (one home, no duplication; DAT-A2's
  fibrewise⟹relative direction is also welcome in this file).
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open TensorProduct

namespace LinearMap

section KerBaseChange

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
variable {M N : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N]
variable [Module R M] [Module R N]
variable (δ : M →ₗ[R] N)

/-- **Purity of the kernel from a flat image**: if `M ⧸ ker δ` is `R`-flat, then the
inclusion of `ker δ` stays injective after tensoring with any module. -/
theorem lTensor_ker_subtype_injective_of_flat_coker
    [Module.Flat R (M ⧸ LinearMap.ker δ)]
    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    Function.Injective ((LinearMap.ker δ).subtype.lTensor A) :=
  lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat (LinearMap.ker δ).mkQ
    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _) (LinearMap.ker δ).subtype
    (Submodule.injective_subtype _) (exact_subtype_mkQ _) A

/-- The map `M ⧸ ker δ → N` induced by `δ`. -/
private noncomputable def barMap : M ⧸ LinearMap.ker δ →ₗ[R] N :=
  (LinearMap.ker δ).liftQ δ le_rfl

private lemma barMap_injective : Function.Injective (barMap δ) := by
  rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_bot, barMap, Submodule.ker_liftQ]
  simp

private lemma barMap_comp_mkQ : (barMap δ).comp (LinearMap.ker δ).mkQ = δ :=
  Submodule.liftQ_mkQ _ _ _

/-- **Purity of the image from a flat cokernel**: if `N ⧸ range δ` is `R`-flat, then
the induced injection `M ⧸ ker δ → N` stays injective after tensoring with any
module. -/
private theorem lTensor_barMap_injective_of_flat_coker
    [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)]
    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    Function.Injective ((barMap δ).lTensor A) := by
  refine lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat (LinearMap.range δ).mkQ
    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _) (barMap δ) (barMap_injective δ) ?_ A
  rw [LinearMap.exact_iff, Submodule.ker_mkQ, barMap, Submodule.range_liftQ]

/-- **Kernel base change from flat cokernels** (the `lm:ctn`-lite keystone, plain
`lTensor` form): if both `M ⧸ ker δ` and `N ⧸ range δ` are `R`-flat, then for any
module `A`, `ker (δ ⊗ A) = range ((ker δ).subtype ⊗ A)`. -/
theorem ker_lTensor_eq_of_flat_coker
    [Module.Flat R (M ⧸ LinearMap.ker δ)] [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)]
    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    LinearMap.ker (δ.lTensor A)
      = LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker δ).subtype.lTensor A) := by
  have hcomp : δ.lTensor A
      = ((barMap δ).lTensor A).comp ((LinearMap.ker δ).mkQ.lTensor A) := by
    rw [← LinearMap.lTensor_comp, barMap_comp_mkQ]
  have hex : Function.Exact ((LinearMap.ker δ).subtype.lTensor A)
      ((LinearMap.ker δ).mkQ.lTensor A) :=
    lTensor_exact A (exact_subtype_mkQ _) (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
  rw [hcomp, LinearMap.ker_comp,
    LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mpr (lTensor_barMap_injective_of_flat_coker δ A),
    Submodule.comap_bot, LinearMap.exact_iff.mp hex]

variable {δ} in
/-- `ker_lTensor_eq_of_flat_coker` in `Function.Exact` form. -/
theorem exact_lTensor_of_flat_coker
    [Module.Flat R (M ⧸ LinearMap.ker δ)] [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)]
    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    Function.Exact ((LinearMap.ker δ).subtype.lTensor A) (δ.lTensor A) := by
  rw [LinearMap.exact_iff]
  exact ker_lTensor_eq_of_flat_coker δ A

variable (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R']

/-- **Kernel base change from flat cokernels, comparison form**: the canonical map
`LinearMap.tensorKer : R' ⊗[R] ker δ →ₗ[R'] ker (𝟙 ⊗ δ)` — the same comparison map as
mathlib's flat-base-change `LinearMap.tensorKerEquiv` — is bijective as soon as the two
cokernels of `δ` are flat (no hypothesis on `R'` at all). -/
theorem tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker
    [Module.Flat R (M ⧸ LinearMap.ker δ)] [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)] :
    Function.Bijective (LinearMap.tensorKer R' R' δ) := by
  constructor
  · intro x y hxy
    have hcoe := congrArg Subtype.val hxy
    rw [LinearMap.tensorKer_coe, LinearMap.tensorKer_coe] at hcoe
    exact lTensor_ker_subtype_injective_of_flat_coker δ R' hcoe
  · rintro ⟨z, hz⟩
    have hz' : z ∈ LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker δ).subtype.lTensor R') := by
      rw [← ker_lTensor_eq_of_flat_coker δ R']
      exact hz
    obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := hz'
    exact ⟨w, Subtype.ext (by rw [LinearMap.tensorKer_coe, hw])⟩

/-- `tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker`, packaged as a linear equivalence
`R' ⊗[R] ker δ ≃ₗ[R'] ker (𝟙 ⊗ δ)`. -/
noncomputable def tensorKerEquivOfFlatCoker
    [Module.Flat R (M ⧸ LinearMap.ker δ)] [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)] :
    R' ⊗[R] (LinearMap.ker δ) ≃ₗ[R']
      LinearMap.ker (AlgebraTensorModule.lTensor R' R' δ) :=
  LinearEquiv.ofBijective (LinearMap.tensorKer R' R' δ)
    (tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker δ R')

@[simp]
theorem tensorKerEquivOfFlatCoker_apply
    [Module.Flat R (M ⧸ LinearMap.ker δ)] [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)]
    (x : R' ⊗[R] (LinearMap.ker δ)) :
    tensorKerEquivOfFlatCoker δ R' x = LinearMap.tensorKer R' R' δ x :=
  rfl

end KerBaseChange

end LinearMap

namespace Algebra.TensorProduct

section RegularBaseChange

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R']
variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]

/-- Multiplication by `f` on `R' ⊗[R] B` is the `lTensor` of multiplication by `f`
on `B`. -/
private lemma mul_includeRight_eq_lTensor_mulLeft (f : B) (x : R' ⊗[R] B) :
    (includeRight (R := R) (A := R') (B := B)) f * x
      = (LinearMap.mulLeft R f).lTensor R' x := by
  induction x with
  | zero => rw [mul_zero, map_zero]
  | tmul r b =>
      rw [includeRight_apply, LinearMap.lTensor_tmul, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply,
        Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, one_mul]
  | add x y hx hy => rw [mul_add, map_add, hx, hy]

/-- **Regular elements stay regular after any base change, from a flat cokernel**
(the DD-1a `hreg` discharge; Kleiman `lm:ctn` (i)⟹(iii) made cheap): if `f` is a
nonzerodivisor of the `R`-algebra `B` and the colength module `B ⧸ (f)` is flat over
`R`, then the image of `f` in `R' ⊗[R] B` is a nonzerodivisor, for EVERY `R`-algebra
`R'` — no flatness of `R'` and no Noetherian hypothesis. -/
theorem includeRight_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_flat_coker (f : B)
    (hf : f ∈ nonZeroDivisors B)
    [Module.Flat R (B ⧸ Ideal.span {f})] :
    (includeRight (R := R) (A := R') (B := B)) f ∈ nonZeroDivisors (R' ⊗[R] B) := by
  have hinj : Function.Injective ((LinearMap.mulLeft R f).lTensor R') := by
    refine LinearMap.lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat
      (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (Ideal.span {f})).toLinearMap
      Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective (LinearMap.mulLeft R f) ?_ ?_ R'
    · intro x y hxy
      simp only [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply] at hxy
      have hsub : f * (x - y) = 0 := by rw [mul_sub, hxy, sub_self]
      exact sub_eq_zero.mp ((mul_left_mem_nonZeroDivisors_eq_zero_iff hf).mp hsub)
    · intro y
      constructor
      · intro hy
        have hmem : y ∈ Ideal.span {f} := by
          rwa [← Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem]
        obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Ideal.mem_span_singleton'.mp hmem
        exact ⟨c, by rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mul_comm, hc]⟩
      · rintro ⟨c, rfl⟩
        have hmem : f * c ∈ Ideal.span {f} :=
          Ideal.mem_span_singleton'.mpr ⟨c, mul_comm c f⟩
        simp only [AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply,
          Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk]
        exact (Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem).mpr hmem
  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_right]
  intro x hx
  have h0 : (LinearMap.mulLeft R f).lTensor R' x = 0 := by
    rw [← mul_includeRight_eq_lTensor_mulLeft R', mul_comm]
    exact hx
  have hz : (LinearMap.mulLeft R f).lTensor R' x
      = (LinearMap.mulLeft R f).lTensor R' 0 := by rw [h0, map_zero]
  exact hinj hz

end RegularBaseChange

end Algebra.TensorProduct

    10	/-!
    11	# Canonical syzygies in a high-window multiplication presentation
    12	
    13	The high-window relation criterion is deliberately stated with a residue-fibre
    14	kernel-spanning hypothesis.  This file constructs the canonical candidate, the
    15	actual kernel of the multiplication presentation, proves it finite, and identifies
    16	its spanning condition with fibrewise injectivity of the injectivized map.
    17	
    18	Flatness of the target cokernel implies that condition.  Conversely, the landed
    19	flattening criterion shows that the condition implies target-cokernel flatness.
    20	Consequently, merely choosing the actual kernel does not evade the nonreduced-base
    21	gate: its fibre-spanning law is equivalent to the flatness one is trying to prove.
    22	No fibrewise image-persistence statement is used as a substitute for this law.
    23	-/

    44	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    45	variable {M N : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N]
    46	  [Module R M] [Module R N]
    47	
    48	/-- Kernel spanning after base change is equivalent to injectivity after first
    49	dividing the source by the global kernel.  This is pure linear algebra and holds
    50	for an arbitrary coefficient module `A`.
    51	
    52	The forward direction lifts through the right-exact base change of the quotient
    53	map.  The reverse direction observes that an element in the fibre kernel has zero
    54	image in the fibre of the injectivization, hence already lies in the fibre image
    55	of the global kernel. -/
    56	theorem ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_iff_liftQ_rTensor_injective
    57	    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
    58	    LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor A) ≤
    59	        LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker f).subtype.rTensor A) ↔
    60	      Function.Injective
    61	        (((LinearMap.ker f).liftQ f le_rfl).rTensor A) := by
    62	  let L := LinearMap.ker f
    63	  have hcomp : f.rTensor A =
    64	      (L.liftQ f le_rfl).rTensor A ∘ₗ L.mkQ.rTensor A := by
    65	    rw [← LinearMap.rTensor_comp, Submodule.liftQ_mkQ]
    66	  have hexact : Function.Exact (L.subtype.rTensor A) (L.mkQ.rTensor A) :=
    67	    rTensor_exact A (LinearMap.exact_subtype_mkQ L) (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L)
    68	  constructor
    69	  · intro hspan
    70	    rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
    71	    intro w hw
    72	    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := LinearMap.rTensor_surjective A
    73	      (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L) w
    74	    have hfx : f.rTensor A x = 0 := by
    75	      rw [hcomp, LinearMap.comp_apply]
    76	      exact hw
    77	    have hx := hspan (LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr hfx)
    78	    rw [← LinearMap.exact_iff.mp hexact, LinearMap.mem_ker] at hx
    79	    exact hx
    80	  · intro hinj x hx
    81	    have hzero : L.mkQ.rTensor A x = 0 := by
    82	      apply hinj
    83	      rw [map_zero]
    84	      have hfx := LinearMap.mem_ker.mp hx
    85	      rw [hcomp, LinearMap.comp_apply] at hfx
    86	      exact hfx
    87	    rw [← LinearMap.exact_iff.mp hexact, LinearMap.mem_ker]
    88	    exact hzero
    89	
    90	variable {P : Type u} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
    91	
    92	/-- An independent boundary presentation of every base-changed kernel makes
    93	the injectivized map remain injective after that base change.  This is the
    94	non-circular bridge from a fibrewise Koszul theorem to the relative flatness
    95	criterion: no flatness of the cokernel is assumed.
    96	
    97	The proof lifts through the right-exact base change of `ker(f).mkQ`.  A lift
    98	in the fibre kernel is a base-changed boundary by `hspan`, and the global
    99	identity `f ∘ d = 0` makes its quotient class vanish. -/
   100	theorem liftQ_baseChange_injective_of_boundary
   101	    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (d : P →ₗ[R] M) (hfd : f.comp d = 0)
   102	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
   103	    (hspan : LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.baseChange S f) ≤
   104	      LinearMap.range (LinearMap.baseChange S d)) :
   105	    Function.Injective
   106	      (LinearMap.baseChange S ((LinearMap.ker f).liftQ f le_rfl)) := by
   107	  let L := LinearMap.ker f
   108	  let fbar := L.liftQ f le_rfl
   109	  have hfcomp : LinearMap.baseChange S f =
   110	      (LinearMap.baseChange S fbar).comp (LinearMap.baseChange S L.mkQ) := by
   111	    rw [← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, Submodule.liftQ_mkQ]
   112	  have hdL : ∀ y : P, d y ∈ L := by
   113	    intro y
   114	    apply LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr
   115	    have hy := LinearMap.congr_fun hfd y
   116	    simpa only [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.zero_apply] using hy
   117	  have hqd : L.mkQ.comp d = 0 := by
   118	    apply LinearMap.ext
   119	    intro y
   120	    rw [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.zero_apply, Submodule.mkQ_apply,
   121	      Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
   122	    exact hdL y
   123	  rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
   124	  intro w hw
   125	  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := LinearMap.baseChange_surjective S
   126	    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L) w
   127	  have hfx : LinearMap.baseChange S f x = 0 := by
   128	    rw [hfcomp, LinearMap.comp_apply]
   129	    exact hw
   130	  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hspan (LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr hfx)
   131	  rw [← hy, ← LinearMap.comp_apply, ← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, hqd,
   132	    LinearMap.baseChange_zero, LinearMap.zero_apply]
   133	
   134	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   135	-- Elaborating the quotient injectivization through tensor purity exceeds the default budget.
   136	/-- Flatness of the target cokernel forces the fibre kernel to be generated by
   137	the base-changed global kernel.  Indeed, the injectivization
   138	`M ⧸ ker δ → N` has cokernel `N ⧸ range δ`; flatness of that cokernel makes the
   139	injectivization universally injective. -/
   140	theorem ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_of_flat_range_quotient
   141	    (δ : M →ₗ[R] N)
   142	    [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)]
   143	    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
   144	    LinearMap.ker (δ.rTensor A) ≤
   145	      LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker δ).subtype.rTensor A) := by
   146	  apply (ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_iff_liftQ_rTensor_injective δ A).mpr
   147	  set fbar := (LinearMap.ker δ).liftQ δ le_rfl with hfbar
   148	  have hfbar_inj : Function.Injective fbar := by
   149	    rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_bot, hfbar]
   150	    exact Submodule.ker_liftQ_eq_bot' _ δ rfl
   151	  have hexact : Function.Exact fbar (LinearMap.range δ).mkQ := by
   152	    rw [LinearMap.exact_iff, Submodule.ker_mkQ, hfbar, Submodule.range_liftQ]
   153	  have hleft : Function.Injective (fbar.lTensor A) :=
   154	    LinearMap.lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat
   155	      (LinearMap.range δ).mkQ (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
   156	      fbar hfbar_inj hexact A
   157	  exact (LinearMap.lTensor_inj_iff_rTensor_inj (M := A) (f := fbar)).mp hleft
   158

## Why I Stopped

The remaining statement is not merely technical. For every residue field and every high-window multiplication map, one must prove

```text
ker(multiplication) = range(Koszul boundary).
```

Only `range ⊆ ker` and multiplication surjectivity are currently proved. The missing reverse inclusion is precisely a relative Gotzmann/first-syzygy theorem, equivalently the unproved finrank lower bound at [DivSchemeHighWindowKoszul.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivSchemeHighWindowKoszul.lean:296).

Choosing the actual global kernel does not bypass this: [DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean:254) proves that its fibre-base-change law is equivalent to the desired quotient flatness, so that argument would be circular.

The old Jacobian flattening theorem changes the base to locally closed rank strata and its Quot endpoint is still sorry-backed. The redesign theorem proves flatness only for the `RZ`-linear reading range, not the larger chart ideal. Neither is a drop-in completion.

Therefore representability is not yet fully formalized. The next substantive task is proving that relative first-syzygy rank estimate, or deliberately porting the full flattening-stratification route.

     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy
     8	
     9	/-!
    10	# Conjugacy transfer for a fibre syzygy presentation
    11	
    12	This file is deliberately independent of the high-window geometry.  It packages the
    13	linear algebra used after a fibre model has been constructed: kernel containment for
    14	the field presentation transfers through three base-change equivalences to the
    15	corresponding relative presentation.  The final corollary feeds that containment into
    16	the `liftQ` injectivity criterion from `DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	set_option autoImplicit false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open scoped TensorProduct
    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    26	
    27	section Conjugacy
    28	
    29	variable {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    30	variable {P M N : Type u}
    31	variable [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
    32	variable [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    33	variable [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    34	variable {P' M' N' : Type u}
    35	variable [AddCommGroup P'] [Module S P']
    36	variable [AddCommGroup M'] [Module S M']
    37	variable [AddCommGroup N'] [Module S N']
    38	
    39	/-- Kernel containment transfers through equivalences conjugating a pair of maps
    40	and their base changes.  The equivalences need not arise from tensor products;
    41	the statement only uses their bijectivity and the two displayed naturality laws.
    42	
    43	`hf` conjugates `baseChange S f` to `f'`, while `hd` conjugates `baseChange S d`
    44	to `d'`.  Thus a witness in the fibre range can be pulled back through the
    45	source equivalence and gives a witness in the relative base-change range.
    46	-/
    47	theorem ker_baseChange_le_range_baseChange_of_conjugate
    48	    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (d : P →ₗ[R] M)
    49	    (f' : M' →ₗ[S] N') (d' : P' →ₗ[S] M')
    50	    (eM : (S ⊗[R] M) ≃ₗ[S] M')
    51	    (eN : (S ⊗[R] N) ≃ₗ[S] N')
    52	    (eP : (S ⊗[R] P) ≃ₗ[S] P')
    53	    (hf : ∀ x : S ⊗[R] M,
    54	      eN (LinearMap.baseChange S f x) = f' (eM x))
    55	    (hd : ∀ y : S ⊗[R] P,
    56	      eM (LinearMap.baseChange S d y) = d' (eP y))
    57	    (hker : LinearMap.ker f' ≤ LinearMap.range d') :
    58	    LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.baseChange S f) ≤
    59	      LinearMap.range (LinearMap.baseChange S d) := by
    60	  intro x hx
    61	  have hfx' : f' (eM x) = 0 := by
    62	    rw [← hf x, LinearMap.mem_ker.mp hx, map_zero]
    63	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hker (LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr hfx')
    64	  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := eP.surjective z
    65	  refine ⟨y, ?_⟩
    66	  apply eM.injective
    67	  rw [hd y, hz]
    68	
    69	/-- The same transfer followed by the relative `liftQ` criterion.  This is the
    70	generic shape consumed by the high-window relation induction: an independent
    71	fibre boundary presentation proves injectivity of the base-changed
    72	injectivization, without assuming flatness of its target quotient.
    73	-/
    74	theorem liftQ_baseChange_injective_of_conjugate_boundary
    75	    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (d : P →ₗ[R] M) (hfd : f.comp d = 0)
    76	    (f' : M' →ₗ[S] N') (d' : P' →ₗ[S] M')
    77	    (eM : (S ⊗[R] M) ≃ₗ[S] M')
    78	    (eN : (S ⊗[R] N) ≃ₗ[S] N')
    79	    (eP : (S ⊗[R] P) ≃ₗ[S] P')
    80	    (hf : ∀ x : S ⊗[R] M,
    81	      eN (LinearMap.baseChange S f x) = f' (eM x))
    82	    (hd : ∀ y : S ⊗[R] P,
    83	      eM (LinearMap.baseChange S d y) = d' (eP y))
    84	    (hker : LinearMap.ker f' ≤ LinearMap.range d') :
    85	    Function.Injective
    86	      (LinearMap.baseChange S ((LinearMap.ker f).liftQ f le_rfl)) := by
    87	  exact liftQ_baseChange_injective_of_boundary f d hfd S
    88	    (ker_baseChange_le_range_baseChange_of_conjugate
    89	      f d f' d' eM eN eP hf hd hker)
    90	
    91	end Conjugacy
    92	
    93	end AlgebraicGeometry

   133	/-- If a map into one ambient submodule has the same underlying values as an

   135	private theorem range_eq_comap_of_equiv_coe
   136	    {F X : Type u} [AddCommGroup F] [Module K F]
   137	    [AddCommGroup X] [Module K X]
   138	    (B A : Submodule K F) (f : X →ₗ[K] ↥B) (e : X ≃ₗ[K] ↥A)
   139	    (h : B.subtype.comp f = A.subtype.comp e.toLinearMap) :
   140	    LinearMap.range f = A.comap B.subtype := by
   141	  ext y
   142	  constructor
   143	  · rintro ⟨x, rfl⟩
   144	    have hx := LinearMap.congr_fun h x
   145	    simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply] at hx
   146	    change B.subtype (f x) ∈ A
   147	    rw [hx]
   148	    exact (e x).property
   149	  · intro hy
   150	    let a : A := ⟨y.1, hy⟩
   151	    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := e.surjective a
   152	    refine ⟨x, Subtype.ext ?_⟩
   153	    have hfx := LinearMap.congr_fun h x
   154	    simp only [LinearMap.comp_apply] at hfx
   155	    change (f x : F) = (y : B)
   156	    calc
   157	      (f x : F) = (e x : A) := hfx
   158	      _ = (a : A) := congrArg Subtype.val hx
   159	      _ = (y : B) := rfl

   133	    (himage : DivUniversalHighWindowFibreImage
   134	      C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j K hO hchi hker n) :
   135	    K ⊗[RZ] ↥Kr[n] ≃ₗ[K]
   136	      ↥(divUniversalFibreHighWindow
   137	        C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j K hO hchi hker n) :=
   138	  (Grassmannian.projectiveQuotientFibreModelEquiv Kr[n]
   139	    (divUniversalHighWindowClosedAmbientFibreEquiv
   140	      (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j K n)
   141	    (divUniversalFibreHighWindowInAmbient
   142	      C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j K hO hchi hker n) himage).trans
   143	    (divUniversalFibreHighWindowInAmbientEquiv
   144	      C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j K hO hchi hker n)

   150	scalar-extending the relation inclusion. -/

   152	theorem divUniversalHighWindowRelationFibreEquiv_coe (n : Nat)
   153	    [Module.Projective RZ (G[n] ⧸ Kr[n])]
   154	    (himage : DivUniversalHighWindowFibreImage
   155	      C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j K hO hchi hker n)
   156	    (x : K ⊗[RZ] ↥Kr[n]) :
   157	    ((divUniversalHighWindowRelationFibreEquiv
   158	        C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j K hO hchi hker n himage x :
   159	      divUniversalFibreHighWindow
   160	        C hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j K hO hchi hker n) :

   169	    divUniversalFibreHighWindowInAmbientEquiv_coe,

    10	/-!
    11	# Multiplication compatibility for the recursive high-window map
    12

    14	`M + n*S`.  It identifies the multiplication map used to define the recursive relation
    15	tower with the generic multiplication map, up to the canonical exponent reindexing.
    16	-/

    19	set_option quotPrecheck false

    39	section HighWindowMulCompatibility
    40	
    41	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    42	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    43	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    44	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi] [IsDominant pi]
    45	
    46	noncomputable local instance instOverCleftHighWindowMulCompatibility :
    47	    C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
    48	
    49	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsIntegral C.left]
    50	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    51	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    52	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
    53	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
    54	variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    55	variable (g : Nat)
    56	
    57	/-- The successor arithmetic identity for the high-window exponents. -/
    58	theorem divUniversalHighWindowExponent_succ (n : Nat) :
    59	    windowS_choice pi hpi g +
    60	        divUniversalHighWindowExponent (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n =
    61	      divUniversalHighWindowExponent (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g (n + 1) := by
    62	  simp only [divUniversalHighWindowExponent, Nat.succ_mul]
    63	  omega
    64	
    65	/-- Reindex divisor-section windows along an equality of exponents. -/
    66	noncomputable def divisorWindowExponentEquiv {p q : Nat} (h : p = q) :
    67	    ↥(divisorSections k (p • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤) ≃ₗ[k]
    68	      ↥(divisorSections k (q • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤) :=
    69	  LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ (congrArg
    70	    (fun e : Nat => divisorSections k (e • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤) h)
    71	
    72	@[simp]
    73	theorem coe_divisorWindowExponentEquiv {p q : Nat} (h : p = q)
    74	    (x : ↥(divisorSections k (p • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)) :
    75	    ((divisorWindowExponentEquiv (C := C) (pi := pi) h x :
    76	        ↥(divisorSections k (q • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)) : C.left.functionField) =
    77	      (x : C.left.functionField) := by
    78	  subst q
    79	  rfl
    80	
    81	/-- Reindex the generic sum exponent to the next campaign high window. -/
    82	noncomputable def divUniversalHighWindowSuccExponentEquiv (n : Nat) :
    83	    ↥(divisorSections k
    84	        ((windowS_choice pi hpi g +
    85	          divUniversalHighWindowExponent (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n) •
    86	            fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤) ≃ₗ[k]
    87	      divUniversalHighWindowSections (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g (n + 1) :=
    88	  divisorWindowExponentEquiv (C := C) (pi := pi)
    89	    (divUniversalHighWindowExponent_succ (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n)
    90	
    91	@[simp]
    92	theorem coe_divUniversalHighWindowSuccExponentEquiv (n : Nat)
    93	    (x : ↥(divisorSections k
    94	      ((windowS_choice pi hpi g +
    95	        divUniversalHighWindowExponent (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n) •
    96	          fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)) :
    97	    (((divUniversalHighWindowSuccExponentEquiv (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n) x :
    98	        divUniversalHighWindowSections (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g (n + 1)) :
    99	      C.left.functionField) = (x : C.left.functionField) :=
   100	  coe_divisorWindowExponentEquiv (C := C) (pi := pi)
   101	    (divUniversalHighWindowExponent_succ (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n) x
   102	
   103	@[simp]
   104	theorem coe_divUniversalHighWindowShiftMul (n : Nat)
   105	    (a : ↥(divisorSections k
   106	      (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
   107	    (m : divUniversalHighWindowSections (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n) :
   108	    ((divUniversalHighWindowShiftMul (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n a m :
   109	        divUniversalHighWindowSections (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g (n + 1)) :
   110	      C.left.functionField) =
   111	      (a : C.left.functionField) * (m : C.left.functionField) := by
   112	  rw [divUniversalHighWindowShiftMul, LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,
   113	    divUniversalHighWindowSuccEquiv, LinearEquiv.coe_ofEq_apply,
   114	    sectionMulBilin_apply_coe]
   115	
   116	/-- The relation-tower multiplication map is generic theta-window multiplication followed
   117	by the canonical successor-exponent reindexing. -/
   118	theorem divUniversalHighWindowShiftMul_eq (n : Nat)
   119	    (a : ↥(divisorSections k
   120	      (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)) :
   121	    divUniversalHighWindowShiftMul (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n a =
   122	      (divUniversalHighWindowSuccExponentEquiv (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n).toLinearMap.comp
   123	        (thetaWindowMul (C := C) (pi := pi)
   124	          (windowS_choice pi hpi g)
   125	          (divUniversalHighWindowExponent (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n) a) := by
   126	  ext m
   127	  rw [coe_divUniversalHighWindowShiftMul, LinearMap.comp_apply]
   128	  change (a : C.left.functionField) * (m : C.left.functionField) =
   129	    ((divUniversalHighWindowSuccExponentEquiv (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n
   130	      (thetaWindowMul (C := C) (pi := pi)
   131	        (windowS_choice pi hpi g)
   132	        (divUniversalHighWindowExponent (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n) a m) :
   133	      divUniversalHighWindowSections (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g (n + 1)) :
   134	        C.left.functionField)
   135	  calc
   136	    _ = ((thetaWindowMul (C := C) (pi := pi)
   137	        (windowS_choice pi hpi g)
   138	        (divUniversalHighWindowExponent (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n) a m :
   139	      ↥(divisorSections k
   140	        ((windowS_choice pi hpi g +
   141	          divUniversalHighWindowExponent (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n) •
   142	            fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)) :
   143	        C.left.functionField) :=
   144	      (thetaWindowMul_coe (C := C) (pi := pi)
   145	        (windowS_choice pi hpi g)
   146	        (divUniversalHighWindowExponent (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n) a m).symm
   147	    _ = _ := (coe_divUniversalHighWindowSuccExponentEquiv
   148	      (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n
   149	      (thetaWindowMul (C := C) (pi := pi)
   150	        (windowS_choice pi hpi g)
   151	        (divUniversalHighWindowExponent (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n) a m)).symm
   152	
   153	end HighWindowMulCompatibility

   155	end AlgebraicGeometry

    11	/-!
    12	# A relative Koszul boundary for high-window relations
    13	
    14	Multiplication by the fixed basis of the `S`-window carries a submodule in
    15	high window `n` toward high window `n + 1`.  Given a target submodule which
    16	contains these products, this file corestricts each basis multiplication to
    17	a step between the two submodules and forms the finite rows-minus-columns
    18	Koszul boundary.
    19	
    20	The next high-window multiplication map kills this boundary.  This is the
    21	relative `range <= kernel` half of the finite-stage relation theorem; the
    22	reverse inclusion on residue-field fibres is the geometric pencil input.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	set_option autoImplicit false
    26	set_option quotPrecheck false
    27	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    28	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 8
    29	set_option maxRecDepth 8000
    30	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false
    31	
    32	universe u
    33	
    34	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
    35	open scoped TensorProduct
    36	
    37	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    38	
    39	open Scheme Grassmannian
    40	
    41	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    42	  Scheme.functionFieldOverModule
    43	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    44	
    45	section HighWindowRelativeKoszul
    46	
    47	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    48	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    49	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    50	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi] [IsDominant pi]
    51	
    52	noncomputable local instance instOverCleftHighWindowRelativeKoszul :
    53	    C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
    54	
    55	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsIntegral C.left]
    56	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    57	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    58	variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
    59	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
    60	variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    61	variable (g r1 r2 : Nat)
    62	variable (b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
    63	  ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
    64	variable (b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k
    65	  ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k ((windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
    66	    + (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)) ⊤))
    67	variable (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
    68	
    69	local notation "RZ" => DivCarveChartRing k
    70	  (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
    71	  (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j
    72	local notation "HS" => ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k
    73	  (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤)
    74	local notation "HI" => Fin (Module.finrank k HS)
    75	
    76	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
    77	-- The dependent source and successor submodules are expensive to elaborate.
    78	/-- The basis multiplications from `K` land in the chosen successor
    79	submodule `Knext`.  Keeping this as a hypothesis also covers the exceptional
    80	seed transition, whose target is not definitionally the recursive range. -/
    81	def DivUniversalHighWindowMulPreserves (n : Nat)
    82	    (K : Submodule RZ
    83	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
    84	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) n))
    85	    (Knext : Submodule RZ
    86	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
    87	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) (n + 1))) :
    88	    Prop :=
    89	  ∀ (t : HI) (z : K),
    90	    divUniversalHighWindowBaseMultiplierTransition (C := C) (pi := pi)
    91	        hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n ((Module.finBasis k HS) t)
    92	        (K.subtype z) ∈ Knext
    93	
    94	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
    95	-- The supported source vector unfolds the dependent multiplication map.
    96	/-- The canonical multiplication-span successor satisfies the preservation
    97	condition by taking a vector supported at the chosen basis index. -/
    98	theorem divUniversalHighWindowMulPreserves_mulSpan (n : Nat)
    99	    (K : Submodule RZ
   100	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
   101	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) n)) :
   102	    DivUniversalHighWindowMulPreserves (C := C) (pi := pi)
   103	      hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K
   104	      (divUniversalHighWindowMulSpan (C := C) (pi := pi)
   105	        hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K) := by
   106	  intro t z
   107	  exact divUniversalHighWindowBaseMultiplierTransition_finBasis_mem_mulSpan
   108	    (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K t
   109	      (K.subtype z) z.property
   110	
   111	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   112	-- Corestricting traverses both dependent high-window ambient types.
   113	/-- Multiplication by one `S`-window basis vector, corestricted from `K` to
   114	a successor submodule known to contain all such products. -/
   115	noncomputable def divUniversalHighWindowBasisStep (n : Nat)
   116	    (K : Submodule RZ
   117	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
   118	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) n))
   119	    (Knext : Submodule RZ
   120	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
   121	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) (n + 1)))
   122	    (hpres : DivUniversalHighWindowMulPreserves (C := C) (pi := pi)
   123	      hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K Knext) (t : HI) : K →ₗ[RZ] Knext :=
   124	  ((divUniversalHighWindowBaseMultiplierTransition (C := C) (pi := pi)
   125	      hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n ((Module.finBasis k HS) t)).comp
   126	    K.subtype).codRestrict Knext (hpres t)
   127	
   128	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   129	-- Reducing the dependent corestriction needs the larger elaboration budget.
   130	@[simp]
   131	theorem coe_divUniversalHighWindowBasisStep (n : Nat)
   132	    (K : Submodule RZ
   133	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
   134	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) n))
   135	    (Knext : Submodule RZ
   136	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
   137	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) (n + 1)))
   138	    (hpres : DivUniversalHighWindowMulPreserves (C := C) (pi := pi)
   139	      hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K Knext) (t : HI) (z : K) :
   140	    ((divUniversalHighWindowBasisStep (C := C) (pi := pi)
   141	        hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K Knext hpres t z : Knext) :
   142	      divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
   143	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2)
   144	        (i := i) (j := j) (n + 1)) =
   145	      divUniversalHighWindowBaseMultiplierTransition (C := C) (pi := pi)
   146	        hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n ((Module.finBasis k HS) t) (K.subtype z) :=
   147	  rfl
   148	
   149	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   150	-- The finite function modules retain both dependent relation subtypes.
   151	/-- The relative finite Koszul boundary between consecutive high-window
   152	submodules. -/
   153	noncomputable def divUniversalHighWindowKoszulBoundary (n : Nat)
   154	    (K : Submodule RZ
   155	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
   156	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) n))
   157	    (Knext : Submodule RZ
   158	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
   159	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) (n + 1)))
   160	    (hpres : DivUniversalHighWindowMulPreserves (C := C) (pi := pi)
   161	      hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K Knext) :
   162	    (HI × HI → K) →ₗ[RZ] (HI → Knext) :=
   163	  finiteKoszulBoundary (fun t =>
   164	    divUniversalHighWindowBasisStep (C := C) (pi := pi)
   165	      hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K Knext hpres t)
   166	
   167	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   168	-- Naming the dependent step family avoids re-elaborating both relation subtypes.
   169	/-- The relative boundary is the generic finite Koszul boundary on its
   170	basis-indexed multiplication steps. -/
   171	theorem divUniversalHighWindowKoszulBoundary_eq_finite (n : Nat)
   172	    (K : Submodule RZ
   173	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
   174	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) n))
   175	    (Knext : Submodule RZ
   176	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
   177	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) (n + 1)))
   178	    (hpres : DivUniversalHighWindowMulPreserves (C := C) (pi := pi)
   179	      hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K Knext) :
   180	    divUniversalHighWindowKoszulBoundary (C := C) (pi := pi)
   181	        hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K Knext hpres =
   182	      finiteKoszulBoundary (fun t =>
   183	        divUniversalHighWindowBasisStep (C := C) (pi := pi)
   184	          hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K Knext hpres t) :=
   185	  rfl
   186	
   187	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   188	-- The row type contains the dependent ambient and relation subtype at one stage.
   189	/-- One component row of the high-window multiplication map. -/
   190	noncomputable def divUniversalHighWindowMulRow (n : Nat)
   191	    (K : Submodule RZ
   192	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
   193	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) n))
   194	    (t : HI) : K →ₗ[RZ]
   195	      divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
   196	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2)
   197	        (i := i) (j := j) (n + 1) :=
   198	  (LinearMap.baseChange RZ
   199	    (divUniversalHighWindowShiftMul (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g n
   200	      ((Module.finBasis k HS) t))).comp K.subtype
   201	
   202	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   203	-- Associating the dependent inclusion with each finite projection is expensive.
   204	/-- The high-window multiplication map is the finite sum of its component rows. -/

   243	    ((windowAddCoherenceUnit (pi := pi) C K p q :
   244	      (relCurve C K).functionFieldˣ) : (relCurve C K).functionField)
   245	  let f := (mul.comp source.subtype).codRestrict target (fun x => by

   248	    rw [map_mulLinear_windowAddCoherenceUnit (pi := pi) C K p q D] at hx

   252	    apply Subtype.ext
   253	    apply mul_left_cancel₀
   254	      (Units.ne_zero (windowAddCoherenceUnit (pi := pi) C K p q))

   256	  · intro y
   257	    have hy : (y : (relCurve C K).functionField) ∈ Submodule.map mul source := by
   258	      rw [map_mulLinear_windowAddCoherenceUnit (pi := pi) C K p q D]
   259	      exact y.property
   260	    obtain ⟨x, hx, hxy⟩ := hy
   261	    exact ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, Subtype.ext hxy⟩

     9	/-!
    10	# Conjugacy transfer for a fibre syzygy presentation
    11	
    12	This file is deliberately independent of the high-window geometry.  It packages the
    13	linear algebra used after a fibre model has been constructed: kernel containment for
    14	the field presentation transfers through three base-change equivalences to the
    15	corresponding relative presentation.  The final corollary feeds that containment into
    16	the `liftQ` injectivity criterion from `DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	set_option autoImplicit false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open scoped TensorProduct
    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    26	
    27	section Conjugacy
    28	
    29	variable {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    30	variable {P M N : Type u}
    31	variable [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
    32	variable [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    33	variable [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    34	variable {P' M' N' : Type u}

    37	variable [AddCommGroup N'] [Module S N']
    38	
    39	/-- Kernel containment transfers through equivalences conjugating a pair of maps
    40	and their base changes.  The equivalences need not arise from tensor products;
    41	the statement only uses their bijectivity and the two displayed naturality laws.
    42	
    43	`hf` conjugates `baseChange S f` to `f'`, while `hd` conjugates `baseChange S d`
    44	to `d'`.  Thus a witness in the fibre range can be pulled back through the
    45	source equivalence and gives a witness in the relative base-change range.
    46	-/
    47	theorem ker_baseChange_le_range_baseChange_of_conjugate
    48	    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (d : P →ₗ[R] M)
    49	    (f' : M' →ₗ[S] N') (d' : P' →ₗ[S] M')
    50	    (eM : (S ⊗[R] M) ≃ₗ[S] M')
    51	    (eN : (S ⊗[R] N) →ₗ[S] N')
    52	    (eP : (S ⊗[R] P) ≃ₗ[S] P')
    53	    (hf : ∀ x : S ⊗[R] M,
    54	      eN (LinearMap.baseChange S f x) = f' (eM x))
    55	    (hd : ∀ y : S ⊗[R] P,
    56	      eM (LinearMap.baseChange S d y) = d' (eP y))
    57	    (hker : LinearMap.ker f' ≤ LinearMap.range d') :
    58	    LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.baseChange S f) ≤
    59	      LinearMap.range (LinearMap.baseChange S d) := by
    60	  intro x hx
    61	  have hfx' : f' (eM x) = 0 := by
    62	    rw [← hf x, LinearMap.mem_ker.mp hx, map_zero]
    63	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hker (LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr hfx')
    64	  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := eP.surjective z
    65	  refine ⟨y, ?_⟩
    66	  apply eM.injective
    67	  rw [hd y, hz]
    68	
    69	/-- The same transfer followed by the relative `liftQ` criterion.  This is the
    70	generic shape consumed by the high-window relation induction: an independent
    71	fibre boundary presentation proves injectivity of the base-changed
    72	injectivization, without assuming flatness of its target quotient.
    73	-/
    74	theorem liftQ_baseChange_injective_of_conjugate_boundary
    75	    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (d : P →ₗ[R] M) (hfd : f.comp d = 0)
    76	    (f' : M' →ₗ[S] N') (d' : P' →ₗ[S] M')
    77	    (eM : (S ⊗[R] M) ≃ₗ[S] M')
    78	    (eN : (S ⊗[R] N) →ₗ[S] N')
    79	    (eP : (S ⊗[R] P) ≃ₗ[S] P')
    80	    (hf : ∀ x : S ⊗[R] M,
    81	      eN (LinearMap.baseChange S f x) = f' (eM x))
    82	    (hd : ∀ y : S ⊗[R] P,
    83	      eM (LinearMap.baseChange S d y) = d' (eP y))
    84	    (hker : LinearMap.ker f' ≤ LinearMap.range d') :
    85	    Function.Injective
    86	      (LinearMap.baseChange S ((LinearMap.ker f).liftQ f le_rfl)) := by
    87	  exact liftQ_baseChange_injective_of_boundary f d hfd S
    88	    (ker_baseChange_le_range_baseChange_of_conjugate
    89	      f d f' d' eM eN eP hf hd hker)
    90	
    91	/-- The conjugate-boundary criterion in the right-tensor spelling used by the
    92	high-window syzygy predicate. -/
    93	theorem liftQ_rTensor_injective_of_conjugate_boundary
    94	    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (d : P →ₗ[R] M) (hfd : f.comp d = 0)
    95	    (f' : M' →ₗ[S] N') (d' : P' →ₗ[S] M')
    96	    (eM : (S ⊗[R] M) ≃ₗ[S] M')
    97	    (eN : (S ⊗[R] N) →ₗ[S] N')
    98	    (eP : (S ⊗[R] P) ≃ₗ[S] P')
    99	    (hf : ∀ x : S ⊗[R] M,
   100	      eN (LinearMap.baseChange S f x) = f' (eM x))
   101	    (hd : ∀ y : S ⊗[R] P,
   102	      eM (LinearMap.baseChange S d y) = d' (eP y))
   103	    (hker : LinearMap.ker f' ≤ LinearMap.range d') :

    16	The two unit-read calculations turn the relative theta killing exponent
    17	`q * S` into a `q`-step shifted transition.  Finally both pinned-chart reads

    78	/-- A shifted high-window ambient section with selected chart read zero is killed
    79	by some later side-preserving transition. -/
    80	theorem exists_divUniversalHighWindowShiftedRelationTransitionOfLE_eq_zero_of_chartRead_eq_zero
    81	    (hb : 0 < windowBound pi hpi) (transitionSide : Bool) (n : Nat)
    82	    (x : G(n + 1))
    83	    (hx : (CR (n + 1) transitionSide) x = 0) :
    84	    ∃ m : Nat, ∃ h : n ≤ m,
    85	      divUniversalHighWindowShiftedRelationTransitionOfLE (C := C) (pi := pi)
    86	        hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j transitionSide n m h x = 0 := by
    87	  let p := divUniversalHighWindowExponent (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g (n + 1)
    88	  let thetaX := (divUniversalHighWindowThetaEquiv (C := C) (pi := pi)
    89	    hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j (n + 1)) x
    90	  have hx' : relThetaResSide p transitionSide le_rfl thetaX = 0 := by
    91	    change relThetaResSide
    92	      (divUniversalHighWindowExponent (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g (n + 1))
    93	      transitionSide le_rfl
    94	      ((divUniversalHighWindowThetaEquiv (C := C) (pi := pi)
    95	        hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j (n + 1)) x) = 0
    96	    exact hx
    97	  have hS : 0 < windowS_choice pi hpi g :=

    99	  obtain ⟨q, hkill⟩ := exists_mul_relThetaSideTransition_eq_zero

   101	  let h : n ≤ n + q := Nat.le_add_right n q
   102	  have hkill_read (readSide : Bool) :
   103	      relThetaResSide (q * windowS_choice pi hpi g) readSide le_rfl
   104	          (relThetaSideUnitSection C RZ pi transitionSide
   105	            (q * windowS_choice pi hpi g)) *
   106	        relThetaResSide p readSide le_rfl thetaX = 0 := by
   107	    have hread := congrArg
   108	      (relThetaResSide (q * windowS_choice pi hpi g + p) readSide le_rfl)
   109	      hkill
   110	    rw [relThetaSideTransition, relThetaSectionsMulLeft_apply,
   111	      relThetaResSide_relThetaSectionsMul, map_zero] at hread
   112	    exact hread
   113	  have hzero_read (readSide : Bool) :
   114	      (CR (n + q + 1) readSide)
   115	          (divUniversalHighWindowShiftedRelationTransitionOfLE (C := C)
   116	            (pi := pi) hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j transitionSide n (n + q) h x) = 0 := by

   118	      _ = (divUniversalHighWindowUnitRead (C := C) (pi := pi)
   119	            hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j transitionSide readSide) ^
   120	            ((n + q) - n) * (CR (n + 1) readSide) x :=
   121	        divUniversalHighWindowShiftedRelationTransitionOfLE_chartRead_pow
   122	          (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j transitionSide readSide
   123	          n (n + q) h x
   124	      _ = (divUniversalHighWindowUnitRead (C := C) (pi := pi)
   125	            hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j transitionSide readSide) ^ q *
   126	          relThetaResSide p readSide le_rfl thetaX := by
   127	        rw [Nat.add_sub_cancel_left]
   128	        rfl
   129	      _ = relThetaResSide (q * windowS_choice pi hpi g) readSide le_rfl
   130	            (relThetaSideUnitSection C RZ pi transitionSide
   131	              (q * windowS_choice pi hpi g)) *
   132	          relThetaResSide p readSide le_rfl thetaX := by
   133	        rw [divUniversalHighWindowUnitRead_pow]
   134	      _ = 0 := hkill_read readSide
   135	  have hthetaY :
   136	      (divUniversalHighWindowThetaEquiv (C := C) (pi := pi)
   137	        hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j (n + q + 1))
   138	          (divUniversalHighWindowShiftedRelationTransitionOfLE (C := C)
   139	            (pi := pi) hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j transitionSide n (n + q) h x) = 0 := by
   140	    refine relThetaSections_eq_zero_of_both_side_reads C RZ pi _ _ ?_ ?_
   141	    · change (CR (n + q + 1) false)
   142	        (divUniversalHighWindowShiftedRelationTransitionOfLE (C := C)
   143	          (pi := pi) hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j transitionSide n (n + q) h x) = 0
   144	      exact hzero_read false
   145	    · change (CR (n + q + 1) true)
   146	        (divUniversalHighWindowShiftedRelationTransitionOfLE (C := C)
   147	          (pi := pi) hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j transitionSide n (n + q) h x) = 0
   148	      exact hzero_read true
   149	  refine ⟨n + q, h, ?_⟩
   150	  apply (divUniversalHighWindowThetaEquiv (C := C) (pi := pi)
   151	    hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j (n + q + 1)).injective
   152	  simpa using hthetaY
